A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same TOHA research work, with 20 readable pages including Appendices A–H. Text extraction, rendered-page comparison and embedded-content checks support a complete comparison.

before.justification: v3.pdf reports original hallucination-detection experiments, baseline comparisons, ablations and annotation analyses in Section 4 and Appendices B and E.

after.justification: v4.pdf retains the same original experimental results, including benchmark ROC-AUC scores, runtime measurements, ablations and annotation analyses.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Algorithm 1 retain identical topological-divergence computation, probe-based attention-head selection and averaging procedures.

E1.justification: Both retain the same MS MARCO, CNN/DM + Recent News, CoQA, SQuAD, XSum and HotpotQA evaluations, together with the full-RAGTruth comparison in Appendix B.2.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is identical in corresponding experiments: SelfCheckGPT, semantic entropy, EigenScore, HaloScope, LLM-Check, perplexity, max entropy and ReDEEP. Appendix B's comparison methods and alternative features also match.

E3.justification: Both specify the same models, 25% test splits, validation size of 100, generation budgets and evaluation metrics. The additional experimental protocols and annotation procedures in the appendices are unchanged.

E4.justification: The prompt-edge and alternative-feature ablations, probe-size and head-count sensitivity studies, transfer tests, copying-head analyses, response-length analyses and annotation checks are identical.

E5.justification: Both report five runs with different data splits, identical uncertainty reporting, and the same independent-sample t-tests and p-values in Appendix B.6 and Table 9.

E6.justification: All numerical and qualitative results match across the main text and appendices. For example, Table 1 retains Mistral-7B TOHA ROC-AUC values of 0.76 ± 0.04 on MS MARCO and 0.96 ± 0.01 on SQuAD.

T1.justification: The divergence definition, entropy/perplexity derivation, Proposition 3.1, and mathematical background, properties and proofs in Appendices C–D are identical.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain identical claims about training-free detection, hallucination-aware heads, competitive performance, efficiency and transferability.

C2.justification: The response-novelty and copying-head interpretations, response-length discussion, model-specific and multimodal limitations, and Appendix H's deployment and manipulation risks are unchanged.

D1.justification: Both provide the same code link, generation and annotation instructions, baseline implementation details, ripser library disclosure and NVIDIA L40 hardware information.

R1.justification: The cited works, reference list and Appendix A are identical, including the positioning relative to existing attention-based detectors and Manifold Topology Divergence.

P1.justification: The first-page arXiv stamp changes from v3 dated 9 Oct 2025 to v4 dated 3 May 2026. All paper prose, author information, terminology and section structure remain identical.

P2.justification: All ten figures, fifteen tables, captions and body layout are identical. Rendered pages 2–20 match exactly; the first-page visual difference is confined to the version/date stamp recorded under P1.

improvement.justification: The scientific content, empirical evidence, proofs, reproducibility information and visual presentation are unchanged throughout both PDFs, including Appendices A–H. Updating the arXiv version/date stamp and associated metadata does not meaningfully improve or diminish paper quality.
